title: Raise the bank surcharge from 3% to 5%
headline: Two points on the bank surcharge. Static, on HMRC's receipts: about £0.9bn.
description: Banks pay a surcharge on top of corporation tax on profits above a £100 million allowance: 3% since April 2023, when it was cut from 8%. HMRC's statistics put the surcharge's receipts at £1.0 billion in 2024-25. Two more points on a 3% surcharge is two thirds more, so the card takes two thirds of that £1.0 billion, £667 million in 2024-25, and grows it with the OBR's onshore corporation tax forecast: about £0.9bn by 2029-30. No behavioural response is allowed for.

baselinePolicy.text: Bank surcharge at 3% on banking profits above a £100 million allowance since 1 April 2023 (8% and £25 million before); receipts £1.0 billion in 2024-25.

source.quote: Bank Surcharge receipts were £1.0 billion in financial year 2024 to 2025, a decrease of £0.5 billion (32.6%) on the previous year, which mostly reflects the full effects of the reduction in the Bank Surcharge rate from 8% to 3% in April 2023 and lower UK banking sector profits

alreadyIncludes: Corporation tax main rate 25% (Rates and allowances: Corporation Tax).

terms.label: Bank surcharge receipts in 2024-25, the first full year at 3%

source.quote: Bank Surcharge receipts were £1.0 billion in financial year 2024 to 2025

terms.label: Two more points on a 3% rate: 2 ÷ 3

source.quote: the reduction in the Bank Surcharge rate from 8% to 3% in April 2023

rawSource.note: Static arithmetic: receipts at 3% scaled up to 5%, then grown with the OBR's onshore corporation tax receipts from 2024-25. HMRC publishes the receipts to £0.1 billion, so the base itself is rounded to within about 10%.

caveats: Static. Banks would shift profits, capital and activity in response; at 8% the surcharge raised £2.0bn to £2.6bn a year, which is not simply 8 ÷ 3 of today's figure. Nobody has certified this number.
HMRC publishes the 2024-25 receipts to £0.1 billion, so the base is rounded to within about 10%; the 2026 edition of the statistics, due in late September 2026, would update it.
The allowance of £100 million (Corporation Tax Act 2010, section 269DE) means only the largest banks pay; the card holds the allowance where it is.

considerations.text: Receipts fell from £2.6bn in 2022-23 to £1.0bn in 2024-25 as the rate went from 8% to 3% and profits fell, which is roughly, but not exactly, in proportion. A rise would recover part of that; how much depends on where banks book profits and hold capital, which HMRC's receipts figure cannot say.

The surcharge applies only to a banking company's profits above its allowance, £100 million since April 2023 (£25 million before). Smaller banks and building societies pay nothing, so the change falls on a few large groups.

interactions.text: Banks pay both: a change to the main rate moves the same profits, and the surcharge figure here is on HMRC's receipts at a 25% main rate.
